title: Public product path not launched: in production '/' is an operator password wall and the marketing landing is served at no URL
expected: An unauthenticated buyer landing on the product's root sees the marketing landing (hero, pricing, trust story, demo CTA) and can begin the 20-min evaluation.
got: The landing/dashboard gate is DEV-ONLY (DEV_GATE = NODE_ENV !== 'production'), so in production '/' always mounts the operator dashboard; the fail-closed proxy then redirects any unauthenticated visitor to the operator password form at /login. /landing and /landing/spark both redirect to '/'. There is no production URL that serves SparkLanding — top-of-funnel is dark, documented as deliberate ('BUILT, NOT LAUNCHED').
scope_note: Explicitly documented as a deliberate descope (docs/DESIGN.md 'Public landing: BUILT, NOT LAUNCHED'; devAuth.ts comment 'top-of-funnel is dark on purpose'). Honesty credited — but the buyer never reads DESIGN.md, and her entire journey happens on this missing surface, so it stays the run's headline ship-bar finding rather than an accepted gap.
l2_priority: Cold-visit the live deploy's root logged out: which surface actually renders at '/' (landing vs dashboard vs login redirect)? Confirm /landing bounces into the gate.
suggested_acceptance: A signed-out production visitor at '/' gets SparkLanding (gate on the real isOperator cookie, not the dev flag); /about, pricing and the demo CTA are reachable without any credential.

title: No marketing-to-pilot conversion path: every CTA dead-ends at the single-operator password login; no signup, no tenant creation, checkout operator-gated
expected: From pricing (or the post-demo peak-intent moment) the buyer can start a pilot: sign up, get an isolated workspace/tenant, and reach checkout — or at minimum leave contact details.
got: All conversion affordances point at /login, which is a single shared operator password ('Enter the operator password') with no account creation. Every pricing tier CTA and the enterprise 'Talk to sales' href is /login; /about 'Start free' goes to /login in prod; the sim's terminal 'Get started — do it with your roles' CTA goes to /login. Workspace creation is refused while tenancy is half-built (KP_MULTI_WORKSPACE locked, ~28 tables workspace-blind), and POST /api/billing/checkout requires an operator session — a demo session is explicitly not an operator. Structurally there is no way for a prospect to become a customer without the vendor hand-provisioning a deploy.
scope_note: docs/DESIGN.md:295-297 names this as a known launch blocker ('pricing / Talk to sales CTAs dead-end at the operator password box'). The blocking dependency is real: opening self-serve tenants before tenancy is scoped would re-open the cross-tenant PII criticals — the fix is sequenced behind tenancy completion, but for the buyer the funnel still ends one click before money.
l2_priority: Follow every conversion CTA live (Start free, each plan CTA, Talk to sales, post-demo Get started) and confirm each lands on the operator password form with no alternative path or contact capture.
suggested_acceptance: At least one conversion path exists from pricing: self-serve signup into an isolated tenant with working checkout, OR an honest pilot-request/contact capture — never the operator password box.

title: The keyless demo is undiscoverable and silently refused: no demo link on /about (the only prod marketing page), and gated deploys bounce /api/demo back to '/' with zero feedback
expected: The product's strongest proof — the keyless guided simulation — is linked from every public marketing surface, and if it cannot run, the prospect is told why instead of being silently returned to where they started.
got: The only link to /api/demo in the codebase is on the unlaunched landing (SparkLanding hero). /about — the one public marketing page in production — has no demo CTA at all (its only actions are Sign in and Start free, both to /login in prod). On a gated deploy without KP_DEMO_ENABLED, GET /api/demo redirects straight back to '/' with no message: the prospect clicks 'Watch the live demo' and lands where they were — indistinguishable from a broken demo, which is this Character's explicit walk-away trigger.
l2_priority: Click 'Watch the live demo' on the live deploy: does it mint the session and auto-start '?sim=auto', or silently bounce? Time the full JD-to-Hired run and note any stall/breakage.
suggested_acceptance: /about carries the demo CTA; a refused /api/demo lands on a surface that says the demo is unavailable (and why/what next) instead of a silent redirect.

title: Demo-session isolation is contradicted by half-built tenancy: with KP_DEMO_ENABLED on a data-holding deploy, an anonymous prospect's session reads the real tenant's rows through ~28 workspace-blind tables (candidate PII included)
expected: The anonymous demo workspace is structurally isolated: a prospect running the guided sim can never read a real tenant's candidate PII, regardless of operator configuration.
got: The demo route's own isolation claim ('never touches the real seeded workspace') only holds for the verified-scoped tables. The candidate pipeline + PII, events, jobs, interviews, decisions and billing tables are workspace-blind, so a minted demo session (a second workspace) reads/writes the first tenant's data through them. The default is safely locked (demoSessionAllowed() = false on gated deploys), but the safety is an env flag plus operator discipline, not structure — KP_DEMO_ENABLED=1 or KP_MULTI_WORKSPACE=1 on a deploy holding real data re-opens the cross-tenant read. The Character's surface binding names exactly this as a compliance finding: reaching real candidate data without auth.
l2_priority: In the live demo session, open Pipeline/Profile/Analytics mid-sim: whose rows render — only SIM-created demo rows, or the seeded workspace's candidates? This is the first question the buyer's Legal team asks.
suggested_acceptance: A demo session provably reads an empty/demo-only dataset on every table (tenancy scoped table-by-table, enforced by assertTenancyReady), so enabling the public demo cannot expose tenant PII under any env combination.

title: The demo's screening 'reasoning' is a canned template: fixed confidence 72, boilerplate strengths, and an offer rationale that claims fit-scaling the code doesn't perform
expected: The guided demo is the buyer's proof that matching is 'reasoned, grounded, defensible' — the reasoning shown should be genuinely computed from the candidate/JD (or clearly labeled as a scripted walkthrough), surviving a pressure-test by a skeptical evaluator.
got: The sim's screening beat writes a hardcoded draft: recommendation 'advance', confidence always 72, rationale 'Strong fit for <jobTitle> — core skills present, seniority aligned', canned strengths, empty red flags — grounding 1/4 (job title only; no CV evidence, no rubric). The offer draft's rationale says 'Salary positioned at the role-band midpoint, scaled by fit' while the code computes a pure midpoint with no fit term. Marketing sets the opposite expectation ('evidence-backed rubric, not keyword bingo'; feature hint: 'it all ships today, no asterisks'). Partial offset: the screen wave carries real reason codes and the group-eval runs the real task machinery with honest timeout states.
scope_note: Deliberate keyless-demo engineering (the spine must run with no LLM key) — but the scripted nature is not disclosed in the demo UI, and the buyer's whole credibility check rests on this beat.
l2_priority: Watch the live screening beat: what reasoning is actually visible (canned draft vs reason-coded wave vs group-eval comparison), and is anything labeled as simulated? Would a skeptical buyer read it as real reasoning?
suggested_acceptance: The demo either computes the screening rationale from the actual sim candidate data (deterministic is fine — show the rubric hits), or visibly labels scripted beats as scripted; no rationale string claims a computation the code doesn't do.

title: 'Talk to sales' opens the operator password form
expected: The enterprise contact CTA captures the highest-intent lead: a contact form, mailto, or calendar link.
got: href='/login' — the org-scale buyer clicks 'Talk to sales' and is asked for the operator password. Subset of EB-H1-02's conversion dead-end, kept separate because it's a distinct mislabeled affordance at the single highest-intent moment (docs/DESIGN.md:296-297 acknowledges it).
l2_priority: Confirm live destination of 'Talk to sales'.
suggested_acceptance: 'Talk to sales' reaches a contact capture (form/mailto/calendar), never an internal login.

title: Off-brand root SEO/OG: the shared link says 'KP Job Fit & Salary Estimator' while every marketing surface brands 'KandiDate'
expected: The link the buyer pastes to Legal/board unfurls with the product's marketing brand and value proposition.
got: Root metadata (title/description/OG) resolves to 'KP Job Fit & Salary Estimator' / 'AI-assisted CV seniority scoring and salary estimation pipeline' (messages meta.title, layout fallbacks), while the landing and /about brand KandiDate with a hiring-pipeline story. /about carries its own correct metadata; '/' (where the landing would launch) does not. docs/DESIGN.md:298-299 lists this among launch blockers ('off-brand Salary Estimator SEO/OG, no sitemap/robots').
suggested_acceptance: The root's title/description/OG match the launched marketing brand; a shared link unfurls as KandiDate with the hiring-pipeline value prop.

title: STRENGTH — Billing correctness is senior-grade: webhook-only entitlement, portal-vs-checkout discipline, honest unconfigured state, customer-favoring edge cases
expected: Money state handled with the care a bank buyer's procurement expects.
got: Entitlement lands ONLY via the signature-verified (standard-webhooks HMAC), idempotent webhook — never from the client; checkout URLs are server-minted and the client only redirects; a customer already on a paid plan changes plans via the provider portal specifically to prevent a parallel-subscription double-charge; configured:false renders an honest 'purchases are disabled' local-dev note; entitlement resolution keeps canceled-but-paid-through customers on their plan and treats past_due with dunning grace; allowance exhaustion degrades to deterministic fallbacks rather than blocking.
l2_priority: Open Billing mid-demo: catalog renders, not-configured note shows, plan CTAs disabled (not erroring); on a configured deploy, verify the checkout redirect + billing=success confirm-poll round-trip.

title: STRENGTH — Reconciliation holds: marketing pricing matches the billing engine 1:1, ROI stats are sourced, and the compliance footnote names its own limit
expected: Claims a skeptical buyer verifies should survive verification.
got: Every landing tier (Free 0/5/1/1-job, Starter 490 Kc 100/5/30min, Growth 1190 Kc 400/20/120min, BYOM 120 Kc unlimited-on-your-keys, 100-min pack 790 Kc) matches plans.ts/PACKS exactly — the same PLANS object the Billing tab renders, so the numbers cannot drift. The enterprise ROI band quotes the buyer's own benchmarks (60-70% screening cut, ~23h manual screening/hire, 40-51h total) with a named source line and a verify-in-product pointer (Analytics -> ROI). The trust section closes with 'this reflects the product's design and controls, not a legal certification' — self-flagged honesty the rubric treats as a strength to keep.

title: STRENGTH — The compliance story a bank buyer needs is public, concrete, and uncontradicted
expected: A public human-in-the-loop / EU AI Act / GDPR Art. 22 story the buyer can hand to Legal.
got: Four dedicated public pillars: human-in-the-loop 'by design, not by a setting'; EU AI Act high-risk framing with meaningful oversight and readable reasoning; GDPR & Article 22 (consent before AI reads data, right to human review, see/erase, 'no solely-automated significant decisions'); tamper-evident exportable audit with calibrated confidence. /about reinforces per-step (fairness gate first, 'AI drafts it. A human signs it.', 'a human on every gate'). A sweep of the landing/aboutPage namespaces found no contradicting fully-automated-decision claim — the hero leads with 'AI for hiring that keeps humans in charge'.
l2_priority: Confirm the trust section renders on the live landing and the wording matches the catalog (en + cs via LandingLangSwitch).
